answer: Graduated trust stops a sybil flood the way a dune stops a tide: a new identity starts with only a marble of weight, tiny and almost nothing, no matter how many accounts one attacker spawns. It earns more influence only through attested, useful work over time, like timber slowly seasoned into a beam. An attacker must fund months of honest-looking labor for each fake before it can sway any decision, while one bad act resets its weight to zero, so scaling fakes costs real time and effort, not just account creation.
